questions.title: Planning an experiment — falling block & rotating disc

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
Diagram: a thin solid disc (radius r, thickness z) on a thin axle, resting on supports (on stands) on a bench; string wrapped around the axle with a block of mass m attached; a light gate (connected to a timer) positioned a distance h below the release point, with h indicated; a vertical metre rule clamped to a stand to measure h.
Procedure and measurements: vary the mass m (independent variable) and measure the speed v of the block (dependent variable) as it passes the light gate, keeping h constant. Determine v from the interrupt length of the light gate (v = length of block/time recorded by the timer). Measure m with a top-pan balance. Measure r with calipers (r = d/2) and z with a micrometer/calipers.
Analysis: plot a graph of 1/v² against 1/m. The relationship is valid if a straight line is produced with a non-zero y-intercept. From 1/v² = πr²z/(2PQhm) + 1/(hP): y-intercept = 1/(hP), so P = 1/(h × y-intercept); gradient = πr²z/(2PQh), so Q = πr²z × y-intercept/(2 × gradient).
Controls: keep h, r and z constant. Identify a fixed starting position (a clamped pin/rod or a fiducial marker on the rule) so h is the same each time. Ensure the axle rotates freely (lubricate the supports, or leave the axle unfixed). Keep the rule vertical with a set square.
Safety: the falling block could damage the bench/block — use a cushion or sand tray; clamp the stands to the bench to prevent them falling. Use a long block to reduce the percentage uncertainty in the interrupt time, and repeat each measurement to average v.

questions.title: Analysis of data — capacitors in parallel & charge sharing

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
EA = V(nC + A), so 1/V = nC/(EA) + 1/E.
gradient = C/(EA) and y-intercept = 1/E

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: Plot the six points of 1/V against n (within half a small square), each with a vertical error bar.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: Draw a straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable line (steepest/shallowest line through all the error bars).

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer: gradient ≈ 0.038 V⁻¹ (from Δy/Δx over more than half the line's length). Absolute uncertainty = gradient of best fit − gradient of worst acceptable line.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.answer: y-intercept ≈ 0.16 V⁻¹ (substituting a point into y = mx + c). Uncertainty = difference between the two intercepts.
